insights.statement: Sales grew, margin fell: revenue rose 7.4% (+€100M) while gross margin fell 1.9 pp, so gross profit stayed flat at €385M — the decline is not a volume problem
insights.decision_relevance: Rules out the volume-led recovery Sales proposes (H1 rejected)
insights.caveat: Fresh (-2.4%) and apparel (-10%) did lose revenue

insights.statement: Electronics, at 11.5% margin (14.9 pp below the group's 26.4%), grew 61% and went from 13.2% to 19.9% of sales; its +€110M is more than the group's +€100M growth, so 1.5 of the 1.9 pp decline is mix
insights.decision_relevance: Locates the problem: electronics pricing and growth policy

insights.statement: Category rates eroded 0.5–1.0 pp in grocery, electronics and apparel (fresh flat), worth 0.4 pp of the decline — a secondary, recoverable driver
insights.decision_relevance: Second lever: promotion and supplier-terms discipline

insights.statement: Freight rose €9M (+23.7%) after the March 2025 carrier contract, but it is booked in operating costs, so it does not explain the gross-margin decline; it is an EBIT lever
insights.decision_relevance: Keeps freight renegotiation in the plan for EBIT but out of the 1.5 pp gross-margin count (H3 rejected)
insights.caveat: Cost classification to confirm with Finance (A004)

insights.statement: Electronics is priced 6% below the main competitor on the top 200 references: closing the gap at flat volume adds €17.4M gross profit, about +0.9 pp of group margin
insights.decision_relevance: Largest and fastest lever toward 1.5 pp
insights.caveat: No elasticity data in the sources; sizing rests on assumption A001 and must be tested

insights.statement: The 2026 budget's +25% electronics growth would cut a further 0.7 pp at today's 11.5% electronics margin, so electronics growth must be made conditional on margin
insights.decision_relevance: The board must reset the electronics growth target for the plan to work
insights.caveat: Scenario A003, other categories held flat

insights.statement: Three gross-margin levers add up to about 1.4 pp — repricing electronics (0.9), restoring grocery and apparel rates (0.3) and recovering fresh and apparel sales (0.2) — just short of the 1.5 pp target, with no store-labour cut
insights.decision_relevance: Sizes the plan against the board target and shows the remaining gap
insights.caveat: Levers sized on the FY2025 base and not fully additive; repricing depends on A001
